SPARTAN: the 6.9.2 text says it applies 'L_1 regularization to the attention patterns', but Table 7 lists its mechanism as 'L_0 regularization on attention'.

Causal scrubbing: 7.4 defines it as a necessity test, with interchange interventions as the sufficiency test. 7.6.6, however, labels a protocol 'Evaluation protocol (Causal Scrubbing)' that also covers sufficiency, interchange and specificity tests.

Gated SAE: 6.2 writes the gate as an indicator (hard threshold), but Appendix C.3 writes it as a sigmoid gate. The recommended Top-k k also differs: 'k = 50–100' in Table 4 versus 'typically 50–200' in Appendix C.4.

Evaluation dimensions differ: 7.6 proposes five (faithfulness, completeness, stability, causal validity, human interpretability), but 15 (proposed-evaluation-framework) proposes four (interpretability, completeness, validity, efficiency). Appendix C.5 'Absorption ratio' also means something different from 'feature absorption' in 6.7.3.
